A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same InfiniCube work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original Waymo-based generation and reconstruction experiments, FID comparisons, ablations and an HD-map-alignment user study (Section 5, Figure 9 and Tables 2–3).

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds an outpainting ablation, a LiDAR simulation demonstration and inference-time/resource measurements in its appendix.

M1.justification: Section 4.3 changes the stated pixel-branch inference frequency from every frame to every four frames. The three-stage architecture, training losses and latent-overlap outpainting procedure remain intact.

E1.justification: Waymo remains the dataset. Appendix C.4 and Figure S16 add simulated LiDAR outputs from generated Gaussian scenes at successive timestamps, extending the demonstrated tasks beyond video generation and scene rendering. v1 already used LiDAR as input geometry, but did not demonstrate this simulation task.

E2.justification: Appendix D introduces vanilla 3DGS optimization as a reconstruction-speed comparator. The Panacea/VISTA video comparisons and the six reconstruction baselines in Table 3 remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds latency/VRAM evaluation with specified single-A100 workloads, including local chunks, a 30,000 m² voxel world and 200-frame videos. The existing Waymo 618/90 split, training budgets, image resolution, user-study procedure and T+5/T+10 novel-view evaluation remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix A.3 and Figure S13 add a qualitative comparison of outpainting with and without reusing overlapping latents, testing continuity at chunk boundaries. The road-surface, guidance-buffer and reconstruction-branch ablations in Figures 7, 9b and 10 are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The existing point-estimate and user-study positive-rate reporting practices are unchanged; the added measurements introduce no uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 2–3 and Figure 9 retain their results. v2 adds outpainting and LiDAR examples plus Appendix D measurements: 30 seconds/20 GB for a local chunk, approximately 6 minutes for a 30,000 m² world, 8 minutes/75 GB for video generation and 10 seconds/45 GB for reconstruction. It reports VISTA at over 12 minutes/70 GB and reconstruction over 100 times faster than vanilla 3DGS optimization.

T1.justification: The latent representations, outpainting equation (1), diffusion objective (S.2), Gaussian-position conversion (S.3) and sky-encoding equation (S.4) are retained. Neither version contains additional theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The main pipeline, controls, scene scale and long-video claims persist. v2 reframes the abstract's gap in prior work from limited scale/inconsistency to indoor applicability/lack of controllability, and explicitly claims reconstruction within seconds in its contribution summary. The 200-frame generation result was already reported in v1.

C2.justification: Section 6 adds a limitation concerning consistency between distant chunks, replacing explicit warnings about restricted geometric diversity, slow multistage sampling and intermediate-failure recovery. Section 4.1 also changes the explanation for road-surface conditioning from sparse map values to incomplete map coverage within local chunks.

D1.justification: v2 identifies the 25-frame SVD-XT backbone and adds detail about coordinate scaling/clamping, bounding-box filtering and inference resources. AdaGN becomes AdaLN, consistent with LayerNorm already specified in v1 Appendix C.3, rather than establishing an architecture change. Conversely, Section 4.1 omits the earlier connected-component and blockwise road-surface construction details.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to MagicDriveDiT, Motion-I2V and DragNUWA while retaining the earlier references. Related work emphasizes longer video generation and describes reconstruction as an adaptation of prior feed-forward approaches, replacing the broader assertion that its capabilities were unmatched by previous approaches.

P1.justification: Substantial rewriting spans the abstract, introduction, related work, method explanations and experimental discussion. A four-item contribution summary and reorganized explanatory paragraphs substantially revise the narrative, although the overall section sequence and much scientific content remain.

P2.justification: v2 adds the outpainting and LiDAR figures S13 and S16, adjusts the pipeline diagram, revises captions and resizes/reflows existing panels. The original color-map, first-frame and user-study figures remain as S14, S15 and S17; table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: The added outpainting ablation and stagewise resource measurements strengthen support for consistency and efficiency claims. Backbone identification and the sky-normalization correction also improve reproducibility. These gains are limited: primary benchmarks are unchanged, LiDAR evidence is illustrative, and v2 removes useful road-construction details and earlier failure caveats. Overall, the added validation and practical information provide a modest net improvement.
